chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

He was asked about a man who bought a bondwoman for a specified price, then sold her and made a profit on her before paying her owner from whom she had belonged. Then her owner came demanding payment from him, so the owner of the bondwoman said to those to whom he had sold her: “Settle this creditor of mine for me, and the profit that I made from you is yours.”
So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.بِثَمَنٍ مُسَمًّى: for a specified and agreed price
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a bondwoman being sold as property in the case described
key_terms.غَرِيمِي: my creditor; the one to whom I owe payment
key_terms.فَرَبِحَ: he made a profit from the resale
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or legal objection
key_terms.يَنْقُدَ: to pay over the price in cash or discharge the payment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to have a purchaser pay off the seller’s creditor as part of a sale arrangement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a sale in which the buyer resells an item before paying the original seller in full. It states that there is no harm in arranging for the second buyers to pay the original creditor directly, while leaving the profit to them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3812 - Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) that

he was asked about a man who bought a bondwoman for a specified price, then sold her and made a profit before paying the original seller.
The original seller came to demand his payment, so the man who sold the bondwoman said to those who bought her: "Take care of this creditor of mine, and the profit I made from you is yours."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in this."
